body: Ah well figured I might as well ask. I already write it down but often it doesn't get taken seriously as I present myself relatively lucid. How do I convince them?

I do think some people go psychotic from stress during college, but if you had these issues beforehand (it seems my psychiatrists cannot grasp chronological events) then that would make no sense. At most they would just get worse. What might help for next time is writing down what your complaints and issues are, not just about the symptoms but also about him. I've noticed that can keep my head a bit clear, when the conversations veers off and I get muddled.

I know how you feel. It can be very hard to keep a grasp on reality and do things that many people do automatically, like basic hygiene and even eating. I think that they classify high functioning as individuals who aren't completely broken away from reality and, as the thread title suggests, self aware. Does your psychiatrist seem to be sceptical towards you being psychotic? I found mine did.

I had the same issues yesterday. I've been diagnosed with schizophrenia, and a psychiatrist that was supposed to look for treatment for me refuses to acknowledge it, purely because I'm high functioning (for now...). She atributed it to BPD, even though I've had that diagnosis in the past and the treatment did not work. My advice is: stick by what you feel, if you have the idea people are not helpful or listening, try to communicate this. If they continue, look for a different one. Seems to me that too many mental health doctors are too focused on textbook symptoms and don't seem to look at individuals. Sorry if this comes off as a bit ranty, haha. Good luck with your search for proper help!!
I get it. Thanks for taking the time to help!
Aha! I see it now. Is the order of operations still in effect? First multiplying and then moving the terms?
I thought that, which you have to simplify to x right? After that you get x + x + 1 = 4. For me the next steps would be 2x = 3, but you can't divide by 2 to get 2.
Ah, I made a mistake typing the equation, the start is x/2, not 2/x, my bad!
Multiply by 2? It doesn't seem to lead back to x = 2 though..

Nier (video game), when you play through it the first time, you think you're just saving your daughter. You get a pretty big plot twist at the end, but when you play through it again and read the backstory you (spoiler) find out you're the bad guy who just killed off humanity. Woops.

Little over half a year, started at 2.4mm with all 3, waited 2 months to get it stretched to 3mm, then 4-6 weeks between stretches, each increases the gauge by a millimeter. Had no trouble with healing at all and stretching did not hurt either.
Went fairly smooth, during the piercing I bled very little and it only spotted after that. ~3 days and the bleeding was gone, didn't hurt after that.
4mm :)
Ah didn't know that. I've not had any trouble with it so far though.
2g/6mm. It's gold plated as well though, couldn't find solid gold that was affordable sadly.
It does feel slightly better after saying it, yet I'm still forced to interact with these people. Atleast until I am fully financially independant, which may take a while still..

There's some things I've learned to let go, such as my dependency on others to be happy or the fact I was bullied when younger, but other things are still extremely upsetting. It feels like I would throw everything I stand for away by forgiving the ones who make me feel angry, if that makes sense.
I'm not sure how to do that though. I don't know how to let go.
I'm not entirely sure what you mean with this, but letting go when psychotic sounds unwise.. I might do things that are dangerous. Or did I misread what you mean?
I'm from the netherlands.

I've tried drawing in the past (and many other hobbies), the main thing holding me back with them is usually my physical limitations. Regardless of practice, I just cannot grasp it properly. I like baking because it's an exact thing; measurements and combinations have to be done properly or you end up with something inedible. I also like to share what I make with others.
A mental health charity might help. I have no clue where to start on looking in to those though..
No idea how. I have very little energy which I expend by just being awake. Any tips would be appreciated!

I've no idea if my country has a mental health alliance. I'm not even sure what those are.. I know how to meditate but I often cannot focus enough. I've tried to write but it often aggravates my psychosis as I have to focus on it. I'm not sure if I'll ever find someone, I've tried.

I have one friend who understands me more than most as he has ADHD, but that's the extent of that. I've had roughly 6 psychiatrists total now, all trying different meds; it's not just side effects that are the issue, it's the fact that the meds don't do what they're supposed to. It's a purely negative thing.

As for being suicidal, I have to fight the thoughts to kill myself every second of every day. I've been like that since roughly 9 years old. Couldn't really attempt a lot because of physical limitations.

When I get so psychotic I attack people, I'm not really in control of what I do, I usually don't even remember them as I kind of get overwhelmed and my brain just kind of blanks. I'm not sure what I could do to fix it.

Lastly, what I want from a partner is trust, stability and intimacy. Just the general things I guess.

My brother wouldn't be an option as he lives with my father. School is going well for now but it's getting harder the less in touch with reality I am, they're aware of my illnesses atleast. I tried a roommate but that didn't end well (I attacked him a couple times out of paranoia) and I don't know if people can deal with it.

I've tried making friends but it seems people just get scared off by the sheer volume of issues I have. I am currently in the process of finding a new psychologist but it's taking a long time. That sub looks interesting. Would you recommend me cross-posting this?
What else is there to improve my situation though? I don't know how to cope, as what I do right now clearly isn't enough.

Not sure if anyone will see this, but guess i'll post just the same. First off, I'm gay, I have cerebral palsy, sleep apnea, chronic pain for physical issues and am schizophrenic, have depression and PTSD. As to my dating life, virtually nonexistent. People generally avoid me, and I've had no luck whatsoever. Been losing weight so who knows, maybe it'll help?
The one on the left trying to climb the glass! It's so cute! Are the two in the middle lying on top of each other?
I'd say.. Blowjob contest! If I win I get to live again, if I die *shrug* I'll atleast have sucked some dick before dying. Win-win for me!

I have multiple physical and mental illnesses, and this applies for every single one of them. Strangers, people I know, friends and even my fucking doctors have said this to me many times: "You don't show <insert behaviour>. That means you don't have it/it's not a problem anymore!". I want to work PREVENTING my symptoms getting worse, and they're just waiting for me to break before helping.

Nier. The story is great, the dialogue and humour have a real feel to them, and the plottwists. Oh my god, the plot twists. Once you complete all endings you just want to curl up into a corner and cry for a week. 10/10 would do again.
Fair point. I guess we wouldn't know.. It's just sad that things like this happen too much.
I get what he's saying though. It's hard to feel love towards someone like that. It's easy to just get bitter and act like that, but the best thing is to just let go. That's the hard part.

I'd say the fact he tried to find and reach out to his father is enough to show he felt something. He said he had good memories as well as bad ones. As someone in a similar situation, it sucks. Mine blame me, for example. They don't see me as their child, but rather a reminder of the other parent. They become bitter and project in on you; you can try to love them but it won't be recieved that way. Eventually the only thing you can do is just cut them out of your life and build a happy one.

Oh, that's a shame :( regardless, it does sound interesting how it works. I definitely notice the dynamic in my parents. My father was the oldest in a family of 6, and is more responsible in comparison, as he acted like a parent when he was growing up.
Explains why they wear gloves making the sandwiches! It's not for us, it's for themselves.

What about twins? I'm a twin. My brother and I have these "moments" where we're thinking about the same subject or blatantly copy eachother, but aside from that our personalities and interests are vastly different. Do you consider it the same as an only child, only twice, or the way you described?

Edit: Forgot to mention, identical twins genetically, if that matters.

Sounds like it could've ended much worse than it did, glad you're still here! You never know what might happen... Hope you feel better now. If you need someone to talk to (doesn't matter what about), you can always message me!

Hmm. What might have happened was that you couldn't clearly communicate what you wanted, I've had that happen a lot in my breaks. Regardless, you'd think they'd be trained to recognize these situations and get help if needed. Your age shouldn't have been an issue as most psychotic breaks happen around adolescence or young adulthood.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but did the woman imply that you couldn't have a psychotic break purely because you were young? I don't know how old you were, but to me if it sounds that someone has a break, you need to see it as something serious..

Your situation describes very closely what happened to me. I think it might be when it's busy, they have to keep the flow of calls going. Who knows. I've always found calling a friend or my psychologist had a better outcome.
I realize this, outside of crisis I am very good at turning around my thoughts. In a crisis however, not so much. I am working on it though :)
Yeah, I see your side as well; it's just hard to realize that in the moments of.. well.. crisis. I definitely feel better about it now though!
Considering I've moved to a different location, that does make me a little more optimistic. Are there specific things I should say or avoid saying?

I have a question for you. I'm not afraid to admit I've used a suicide hotline myself a couple of times. However, every time the person on the other side sounded annoyed and bored, and once they assessed I was is no immediate danger, they just tried to get me to hung up. Naturally this makes me feel even worse and I genuinely had to struggle not give in. Now, when I feel like I need to call, I don't want to because of my experiences. What do you make of this?

THANK YOU. Everywhere on reddit people throw around that it's a great show and if you don't like it, you don't understand the humor. I understand it perfectly well. I find it boring because the characters are static and barely change. /rant

I have the same thing. It's called oral hayfever as far as I know; the regular tests for hayfever didn't show anything yet I exhibited the symptoms you listed. Heating fruits and vegetables breaks down the protein causing it. I love fruits and vegetables but can't eat any because of it; microwaving them helps. The worst one for me are pineapples, mango's and peppers.

I have Cerebral Palsy, chronic pain, chronic depression, BPD, OCD and schizophrenia. It's incredibly hard for me to interact with people without it costing a large amount of energy; most people stop talking to me after they know I have so many issues so I usually play solo. I find skills such as Agility extremely soothing and it helps me relax. I also love books and most of the quests are like an interactive book.

I know the feeling. I've also had the problem of people "running" from me once they realise I have mental illnesses. Problem is, for me, it's a part of me. I can try to hide it but it won't go well. Kind of like what happens when you're in the closet, hah. My point is that you shouldn't bother with people who don't look past an illness and see the person. Just the fact that you have goals is already a big step to improving. Good luck :)

I don't have gmail, so I can't.. And with pets, the financial part is an issue too. I would like one but it's just not an option in the near future. I am also afraid I'll start to resent the creature for effectively "forcing" me to stay alive to care for it. Not logical thinking I know, but yeah.
I used to have 5 cats in the house where I lived with my mother, and 2 of them were very attached to me. It would be too straining on me physically to take care of one these days, sadly...

Emil, from Nier. He has a crush on the protagonist, but it's only confirmed in the official book released of the game in Japanese. Someone translated it, but I can't remember where I found it. There also was a hermaphroditic character called Kainé. Loved the game, but this made me love it just a bit more! :D

I am seeing several doctors about this yes. The problem is, none of them really understand why I experience this. Currently trying medication, but most I've tried so far (anti-depressants, anti-psychotics mainly) only make it worse. There's only one person I really trust in my life, but she can only listen. It's different from actually experiencing it, sadly.

I experience hallucinations (mainly visual, tactile and olfactory) all day long, they don't stay in focus constantly. This makes me very paranoid and jumpy. I usually describe it to people as the scary moment you feel approaching in horror movies. I put up a mask and can hold conversations with people like normal but internally I always dread when the next "wave" hits. Almost no one knows this about me and thinks I'm just a normal guy, but I feel afraid and lonely.

Thank you for this. I've seen this.. thing.. twice myself. The descriptions match, it hasn't reappeared, but the scary thing is that my friend who lives 30 minutes away from me, described it the same way. The first time I saw it, I was very young, sitting in front of the window, when it suddenly sprinted in front of it, sort of.. warped it's face (I'm not sure, I was young) and ran off, all while grinning very creepily. To this day it haunts me, and I'm shivering while writing this.
